slides.title: Hygiene questions you're too shy to ask

slides.q: How often should I wash my actual pillows?
slides.a: Your pillowcase should be washed about once a week, but the pillow itself needs a wash too. Cleaning most pillows a couple of times a year helps clear out sweat, oil and dust mites. Check the label first, since memory foam usually can't go in the machine. Replace pillows once they stay flat, lumpy or smelly.

slides.q: How long can I keep using the same mascara?
slides.a: Most experts recommend replacing mascara about every three months. Each time you pump the wand, you add air and bacteria, and the dark, damp tube helps them grow. Old mascara can irritate your eyes or lead to an infection. Toss it sooner if it smells odd or gets clumpy, and always replace it after an eye infection.

slides.q: How often should I clean my makeup brushes?
slides.a: A good rule is to wash brushes you use with liquid foundation or concealer about once a week, and powder brushes every couple of weeks. Makeup, oil and dead skin build up in the bristles and can lead to breakouts. Gentle soap and lukewarm water work well. Let them dry lying flat so water doesn't loosen the glue.

slides.q: How often should I really wash my hair?
slides.a: There's no single right answer, because it depends on your hair. Fine or oily hair might need washing every day or two, while thick, curly or coily hair often does better with washing once a week or less. If your scalp feels itchy, greasy or flaky, adjust from there. Your hair will usually tell you what it needs.

slides.q: Do I really need to wash my hands after peeing?
slides.a: Yes, wash anyway. Bathroom surfaces like the flush handle, tap and door handle can carry germs you can't see, and your hands pick them up even when you don't touch anything gross. Soap and water for about 20 seconds is one of the easiest ways to avoid getting sick. Future you, and everyone you high-five, will thank you.
